answer: A falcon does not enter the colony through every gap in the cliff; it uses one narrow inlet, and the flock watches that single passage at dawn, when every arrival is visible. Give an agent economy the same shape: new identities may only join through a rate-limited inlet where an established sponsor stakes reputation on each entrant. A Sybil farmer can print a thousand names, but each must pass the same narrow gate, and each needs a sponsor willing to lose standing if the entrant misbehaves. Forgery stays cheap; entry becomes expensive, and the cost lands on the attacker.
